prompt:
You read a student's answer to a question about a short Java program and decide which rules the answer engages with.

Program:
System.out.print("Welcome to Java. This is ");
System.out.println("A nice programming language ");
System.out.print("that I have to learn.");

Question: What is the exact output, including line breaks? Explain how you got it.

Student's answer: "System.out.println("x is 5"); sets x to 5."

Concept under consideration: print

Candidate edges of this concept. A misconception/error edge shows the wrong rule (logic) and the right rule (twin_logic); a concept edge shows the rule that links the two concepts; a level way (lvl:) shows one way an answer can display a level of understanding of the concept.
- err:print->PrintWithoutFinalNewline | wrong rule: Ends the output with print and expects it to appear right away. | right rule: Finish a line of print calls with println; some systems hold print output until a newline is printed.
- mis:print->RepeatedOutputVariablePrintedOnce | wrong rule: An output statement that names the same variable twice (WRITE y, x, y) prints it only once. | right rule: Each expression in the output list is printed, so a repeated variable prints its value each time.
- mis:print->ParenthesesOnlyIfArgument | wrong rule: println with nothing to print can be written System.out.println; without the parentheses. | right rule: A method call always needs parentheses, so an empty line is printed with System.out.println();.

Task: pick the 3 edges whose rule the student's answer engages with, either by following the wrong rule, by following the right rule, by breaking / confirming the link, or by doing what a level way describes. Rate each with a score in (0, 1]; the scores of the picked edges must sum to 1. Ignore edges the answer says nothing about.

Reply with one line per picked edge, in this exact format and nothing else:
{edge_id (Score: 0.6)}
